s: A manufacturer must keep sensor data processing inside its factories for data residency reasons, using servers it already owns. The company already runs containerized workloads on Amazon ECS in AWS and wants to use the same ECS APIs, task definitions and console to deploy and monitor the factory workloads. The factory workloads are batch jobs that need no inbound traffic, and the factories have reliable outbound internet access. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
o: Use Amazon ECS Anywhere. Install the AWS Systems Manager Agent and the ECS agent on the factory servers, register them as external instances in an ECS cluster, and run the tasks with the EXTERNAL launch type.
Order AWS Outposts racks for each factory and run the ECS tasks on the Outposts.
Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the factory servers and convert the ECS task definitions to Kubernetes manifests.
Install AWS IoT Greengrass on the factory servers and repackage the containers as Greengrass components.

w.y: ECS Anywhere registers on-premises servers or VMs as external instances in an ECS cluster, so the same ECS control plane, APIs and task definitions run work on the company's own hardware. The servers need outbound access to AWS endpoints. Load balancing and the awsvpc network mode are not supported on external instances, which does not matter for batch jobs without inbound traffic.

o.A: Correct. Same ECS tooling, existing servers, data processed on site.
o.B: Outposts would work but means buying new AWS hardware for every factory instead of using servers the company already owns.
o.C: EKS Anywhere is Kubernetes, not ECS; the workloads would have to be converted and a new platform learned.
o.D: Greengrass targets edge devices and IoT logic. It is not the ECS control plane, so the team loses its ECS APIs and console.
